The '''Lol sector''' was a [[Sector/Legends|sector]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. Located within its boundaries were the [[Planet/Legends|planets]] [[Kendamar]] and [[Majilop]], as well as the [[Lol system/Legends|Lol system]], home of the [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Sumria]] [[Species/Legends|species]]. The sector was one of five sectors in which the [[Tenloss Syndicate/Legends|Tenloss Criminal Syndicate]] was active.

==Description==
The Lol sector was a [[Sector/Legends|sector]] of [[Realspace/Legends|space]] located in the south-west portion of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. It neighbored the [[Merel sector/Legends|Merel sector]] on its rim-ward border, and, clockwise from there, bordered the [[Skine sector/Legends|Skine]], [[Dail sector/Legends|Dail]], [[Astal sector/Legends|Astal]], [[Kibilini sector/Legends|Kiblini]] and [[Tolonda sector/Legends|Tolonda sectors]]. Between the Tolonda and Merel sectors, the Lol sector bordered part of [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]].<ref name="EAOC" />

Located within the Lol sector were the [[Dom-Bradden system/Legends|Dom-Bradden]], [[Drexel system/Legends|Drexel]], [[Kendamar system/Legends|Kendamar]], [[Lol system/Legends|Lol]], and [[Majilop system/Legends|Majilop systems]].<ref name="EAOC" /> The Bradden system contained the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Dom-Bradden/Legends|Dom-Bradden]], [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Affytechan]]s, a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Plant/Legends|vegetable]] [[Species/Legends|species]].<ref name="COJ" /> The Drexel system contained a single planet, a [[Water/Legends|water]] world eponymously named [[Drexel/Legends|Drexel]]. Drexel was [[Orbit/Legends|orbited]] by [[Three Moons (Drexel)|Three Moons]] which were incorporated into oaths of the planet's [[Human/Legends|Human]] inhabitants. These Humans were exiled to the world by [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]], and created a society built on floating structures. The Human immigrants shared the world with the native [[Sea-dragon]]s, and some the of the Humans developed a mutually beneficial relationship with the Sea-dragons.<ref name="M12" /> The Lol system was also home a sentient species; the [[Sumria]]s.<ref name="ISB" /> The Kendamar system and Majilop systems both contained an inhabited world of the same name; [[Kendamar]] and [[Majilop]], respectively. Both planets housed criminal organizations associated with the [[Tenloss Syndicate/Legends|Tenloss Syndicate]].<ref name="GG11" />

==History==
The region was explored sometime between [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]] and [[25 BBY/Legends|25 BBY]]. Too distant, it was never part of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="TEA" /> The Lol sector eventually became a sector of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].<ref name="EAOC" />

[[File:Kendamari_Casinos.svg|thumb|right|200px|The [[Kendamari Casinos]].]]
The planets Kendamar and Majilop both housed criminal groups affiliated with the Tenloss Syndicate. The Tenloss Syndicate was one of the largest non-[[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] criminal organizations in the Rim, having spread from the [[Bajic sector/Legends|Bajic sector]] into not only the Lol, but also the Astal, Dail, and Skine sectors. In the Lol sector, its businesses included the [[Kendamari Casinos]] operating out of Kendamar, which provided a chain of [[Gambling/Legends|gambling]] facilities throughout the sector, catering for upper-class clientèle. They also sponsored sporting events, such as annual [[sun jammer]] [[Sun jammer racing|races]], drawing prospective gamblers from neighboring sectors. Despite Tenloss' independence, a number of the more prosperous [[Casino/Legends|casinos]] were rumored to be controlled by Hutt operatives. The planet Majilop was home to the [[Lucin Syndicate]], a Tenloss-affiliate, and a major producer and distributor of illegal [[Pornography|holoporn]] to the Rim.<ref name="GG11" /> The sector also saw frequent activity by the [[Ragnar Syndicate]], a large [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] syndicate originally founded in the [[Merel sector/Legends|Merel sector]].<ref name="GG9" />

==Inhabitants==
The [[Sumria]]s were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] from the planet Lol. The members of the Sumrian [[thought-caste]] had four digits on each hand; consequently, they developed a base-eight measurement system. This gave rise to the [[Df]], a unit of measurement used to categorize artillery, which was one of three systems in wide use by the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]].<ref name="ISB" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Lol sector was first named in ''[[Galaxy Guide 9: Fragments from the Rim]]'', a [[West End Games]] [[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game|roleplaying]] sourcebook published in [[1993]]. However, the name Lol itself was first used in the ''[[Imperial Sourcebook]]'' published in [[1989]], in relation to the Lol system. The [[Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion|online companion]] to ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed two new systems within the Lol sector. This incorporated events from the [[Marvel Comics]] [[Star Wars (1977)|''Star Wars'']] series of [[1978]], along with events from the [[Bantam Spectra]]'s [[1995]] novel [[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']].

Other ''Star Wars'' [[canon]] had established the planet [[Drexel II]]. [[Jason Fry]] distinguished this from the planet Drexel seen in the Marvel comics by the creation of the [[Drexel Minor system/Legends|Drexel Minor system]], excluding those events from the coverage of this article.<ref name="Jason Fry Drexel">{{JCFCite|url=posts/30387023|board=Literature|thread=The Essential Atlas and Galactic Cartography: Official Discussion|user=[[Jason Fry|jasonfry]]|date=2009-08-28|time=11:05 PM|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180225165344/http://boards.theforce.net/threads/the-essential-atlas-and-galactic-cartography-official-discussion.21938930/page-109}}</ref>
